brief.headline: Push Silk Polypack toward ₹205/kg (bottom of the market band for pharma laminates) and ask for 15 extra days of credit to free up ₹320 cash for us.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a price close to ₹205/kg, the bottom of the market band for pharma laminates.
priceAsk.basis: The open market for pharma/ORS sachet laminates runs ₹205–305/kg, and we should aim for the lower end; the underlying BOPET film imports land at 171.60 ₹/kg, so there's room below the top of the band.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Ask for 45 days after receipt (15 more than today's 30).
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹320 freed up for us if we stretch by another 15 days.

brief.financialLeverage: Silk Polypack publishes no financials, so we can't see how healthy or cash-tight they are. Our ₹7775 annual spend is tiny, which means we're not a must-keep account for them — so we can't push as hard as with a bigger supplier. Because their finances aren't public, we lean on the market price band and on lining up a proven second source to create our leverage.

evidence.point: Our total annual spend with them is very small
The open market for pharma/ORS laminate sachets runs in a band
Typical market price for this laminate is
Underlying BOPET film imports land at
Extending payment terms by 15 days would free up cash for us

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: A listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC in tiny volumes — proven and scalable for laminate sachets.

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: A listed flexibles giant that makes both the film substrate and does conversion — can second-source at scale.

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: The India arm of the global Constantia group, making pharma blister and sachet laminates — a strong second source.

risks: Our spend is only ₹7775 a year, so we have almost no volume leverage — they may not care if we walk.
Silk Polypack's financials aren't public, so we're flying blind on their cash situation and can't tailor the ask to their borrowing cost or distress.
We don't know our own average price or best price for laminates from other suppliers, so we can't prove an internal gap — only cite the market band.
If we squeeze too hard on a small supplier with no financial transparency, they may just decline the business rather than negotiate.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about moving our laminate price closer to ₹205/kg — the bottom of the market band we're seeing — and extending terms to 45 days to help our cash flow.
